clue.text: Wife rings notorious mistress over in Jersey

parts.note: two rings are two O shapes

indicators.note: over signals that the mistress's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Nell Gwyn, the famous mistress of Charles II

explanation.surface: A tale of a wife and a royal mistress somewhere on the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Jersey' looks like the Channel Island; the definition is a jersey, the knitted garment. 'over' turns NELL into LLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen is a knitted garment such as a sweater, and a jersey is exactly that kind of pullover.

clue.text: Clapped-out Cortina, one missing temperature instrument

indicators.note: a clapped-out car is wrecked, so the letters of the car's name are knocked into a new order
missing tells us a letter is lost from the car's name

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: An old Ford Cortina has broken down with its temperature gauge gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes T from CORTINA to leave CORINA; 'Clapped-out' shuffles CORINA plus A. The Cortina was a popular British family car.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, so it is one example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Left Scotch for one German telling stories

parts.note: in Scots dialect the word for one is yin

explanation.surface: Someone abandons whisky for a German drink while spinning a yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky but means the Scots dialect, where 'one' is YIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a gentle idiom for being untruthful, which is what fibbing or deceiving someone means.

clue.text: Like some bands? Go on with one in the City

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the City's letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
to go on is to continue or endure, i.e. last
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about bands, then advice to carry on working in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' suggests music groups but means rubber bands. The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber bands stretch and spring back, so some bands are describable as springy and stretchy.

clue.text: Penniless, break out and dash back to mother

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembled string is read in the opposite direction
penniless means without the P that stands for penny

parts.note: to break out is to erupt
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A broke escapee breaks out and hurries home to Mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penniless' removes the P for penny, leaving ERUT; 'back' then reverses the whole string. 'mother' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother someone is to care for and raise them, which is to foster or rear them.

clue.text: College, which in Paris has no peers

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the adjective for something that has no peers

parts.note: UNI is short for university, a college
que is French for which

explanation.surface: A college that, in Paris, stands without equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has no peers stands alone and without equal, the sense of being one of a kind.

clue.text: Puts in parts that naturally fit old printer's output?

definitions.text: Puts in parts that naturally fit
definitions.meaning: a director who gives actors roles matching their natural character
a printer of old made metal letters cast in moulds

explanation.surface: A director's casting choices set beside a printing workshop's products.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TYPE CASTS for the second reading: hot-metal type was cast in a foundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting performers in roles matching their personality is the theatrical sense; pieces of cast metal type are the printing sense.

clue.text: Romanov leader thrilled to be from same family

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: thrilled means elated

explanation.surface: The head of the Romanov dynasty is delighted to be among royal kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives belong to the same family, so being kin by blood is what this word expresses.

clue.text: Old PM tackled issues in novel

indicators.note: tackled is read as took on or grappled with, so the prime minister's name grips the other piece

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782
issues means hands out, distributes

explanation.surface: A former prime minister dealt with problems in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: HANDS OUT sits between NORT and H. Lord North led Britain during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell's 1855 book about industrial Manchester bears this title, so it is a classic Victorian novel.

clue.text: Arab channel now received in smart part of London

indicators.note: received in means the other piece is taken inside

parts.note: W1 is the postcode of London's fashionable West End, with the 1 read as I
AD, anno domini, is the present era, i.e. now

explanation.surface: An Arabic TV channel is now available in London's fashionable West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' looks like broadcasting but means a watercourse. W1 is the postcode covering Mayfair and the West End.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry riverbed in Arabia or North Africa that runs with water only after rain, so a watercourse or channel.

clue.text: During a catnap I start to conceive hot rods here

indicators.note: During signals that the following pieces sit inside the cat nap

parts.note: split as cat (a tom is a male cat) and nap (the nap of carpet is its pile)

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: While napping I dream up an idea for souped-up cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catnap' must be split into two words, cat and nap, and the I plus C sits between them. 'hot rods' suggests fast cars but means radioactive fuel rods.
explanation.definitionFit: An early name for a nuclear reactor, where radioactive fuel rods get hot as fission proceeds.

clue.text: A little invention creates first of goals in extra time

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: a wide is a cricket extra, a run given for a ball bowled out of reach

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A late goal in extra time sounds like a football match's dramatic finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra' looks like football's extra time but is cricket's WIDE, a run awarded when the ball is bowled out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gadget or contrivance, often one whose name the speaker cannot recall, is a little mechanical device.

clue.text: Tense old character keeps pet trim

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: keeps is read as holds or retains within, so the old character wraps round the pet

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet
a cat is a typical pet

explanation.surface: A nervous ancient figure keeps a pet well groomed.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim something is to cut it short, which is to shorten or curtail it.

clue.text: Watch kept here as quoted scrap firm ends in defeat

indicators.note: as quoted means as spoken, so we use a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: scrap material is waste
CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: ends in means the closing letters of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: A scrapyard firm finally goes under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb but is a pocket watch, traditionally kept in a fob pocket of this garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocket watches were carried in a small pocket of a man's sleeveless vest worn under a jacket.

clue.text: After strike's lifted, rebel works for buttons

indicators.note: After places the rebel anagram following the reversed piece
lifted in a down answer means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to lam is to thrash, so strike's (strikes) gives lams

indicators.note: works signals the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Once a strike is called off, the rebel goes back to work for very little pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns LAMS up to SMAL; 'works' rearranges REBEL as LBEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is something trivial or worth very little, and buttons is slang for a paltry, trifling amount.

clue.text: Out-of-the-way holiday destination top couple left

indicators.note: top couple left means the first two letters are departed, removed

parts.note: the seaside is a classic British holiday destination

explanation.surface: An off-the-beaten-track holiday spot that a couple at the top have left.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside is to put it out of the way, the adverbial sense of to one side.

clue.text: God knows, bank margins have dropped

parts.note: wot is an archaic form meaning knows, as in God wot

indicators.note: the margins are the outer letters, which are removed to leave the middle

explanation.surface: Heaven knows how the bank's profit margins have fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God knows' reads as an exclamation; God is the definition and knows is archaic WOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief deity of Germanic mythology, Odin under his German name, used by Wagner in the Ring cycle.

clue.text: Former writer's pursuing goal in Old English

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the abbreviation
pursuing means following behind, so the writer's piece comes after

parts.note: the net is the goal in football
the writer is I, so writer's means I am, I'M

explanation.surface: An author chases a goal in an Old English setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' stands for 'writer is', the writer being the setter: I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Onetime is an adjective meaning previous or erstwhile, so it can replace former.

clue.text: He's written to Dad, nervous about Sunday's match

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: re means about, concerning
S is short for Sunday
to see a bet in poker is to match it

explanation.surface: A letter to Dad, who is anxious about Sunday's game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' is not a game here but the poker sense: see a stake by matching it.
explanation.definitionFit: The recipient of a letter is the person written to, the one whose name goes on the envelope.

clue.text: Woman's upset about old DG's reincarnation

indicators.note: about means around, enclosing the other piece
upset in a down answer means turned upside down, reversed

parts.note: her is a woman's pronoun
John Birt was Director-General of the BBC in the 1990s

explanation.surface: A woman is upset about a former Director-General being reborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns HER into REH. DG is Director-General, here of the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born again in a new body is what reincarnation means, a second birth.

clue.text: Doctor learnt to bypass hospital entrance

indicators.note: to bypass is read as to go around, so the jumble surrounds the other letter
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A medic learnt to avoid the hospital's front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges LEARNT into ENTRAL, which goes round H. 'entrance' is the verb, to captivate, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or hold them spellbound, the same sense as to charm utterly.

clue.text: Second refusal to admit current state in Med

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, enclose

parts.note: no is a refusal
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A second refusal to let in electricity in a Mediterranean country.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny principality on the Riviera coast is a sovereign country on the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Our lot will be enough to put in flush

indicators.note: put in signals the word to is inserted into the other pieces

parts.note: our lot is we, so our lot will is we'll
to do is to suffice, as in that will do

explanation.surface: Our group will have enough to fill the toilet cistern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' suggests a toilet but means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means having plenty of money, so wealthy or comfortably off.

clue.text: Carpet free? Large one's dumped

indicators.note: dumped means thrown out, removed from the word

parts.note: to free is to liberate
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A free rug, with the big one discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb, to scold someone, as in being carpeted by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to reprimand them severely, which is to scold or rebuke them.

clue.text: Contrarily, some womanisers pine for it, maybe

indicators.note: contrarily means in the opposite direction, so the letters are read backwards
some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Some womanisers, perversely, long for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like a verb, to long, but is the tree, a source of sticky sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine trees exude a sticky sap that hardens, so a pine is an example source of this substance.

clue.text: In season, I wonder about binman in restaurant

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces go inside the season

parts.note: winter is a season

indicators.note: about means turned around, reversed

parts.note: wonder means awe

explanation.surface: A diner muses on why a refuse collector is in the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses I plus the synonym to EWAI. A binman is a British refuse collector, but here the bins are racks for wine bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: The restaurant sommelier looks after the wine stored in racks called bins, so is a playful binman.

clue.text: Big horse kicks another breed

indicators.note: kicks means kicks out, removes

parts.note: the Shire is a large British draught horse
another horse: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A big horse kicks out at a horse of another breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another horse, slang for heroin, which is H.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire offspring is to father them, which is to breed or beget.

clue.text: Dams eat the same nuts

indicators.note: eat means take inside, enclose

parts.note: weirs are low dams across rivers
do is short for ditto, the same

explanation.surface: Mothers eat the same kind of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dams' suggests mothers of animals, but means barriers across rivers. 'nuts' is a plural noun, crazy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts as a noun means eccentric or crazy people, i.e. oddballs.

clue.text: Stones' hit originally breaks record

definitions.note: a plural possessive used as a collective noun for stones

indicators.note: breaks means enters, splitting the word

parts.note: a single is a record

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones' first hit breaks a sales record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' looks like the band but means pebbles on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles found on beaches, i.e. a collection of stones.
